data.hypothesis: Processing up to eight independent options in contiguous lanes should let the compiler SIMD-vectorize the numerous rollback updates without changing each option's terminal-power exponents, rollback order, or arithmetic expression. The previous attempt did not compile because std::min received an enum and an int; this experiment fixes that type mismatch. Full-call measurement is needed to determine whether SIMD throughput outweighs batching and scratch costs.
data.notes: The prior attempt (6ffd5d83eb5045bc-h01) failed at build time on the std::min argument-type mismatch, so it provides no vectorization or timing result. This candidate fixes that mismatch and leaves the SIMD mapping otherwise intact. The valid baseline mean was 0.3909827 seconds; no candidate timing or correctness result is available yet.
transformations: Pack independent inputs into batches of eight with lane-contiguous state and scratch storage.

Apply OpenMP SIMD directives across lanes in initialization, terminal-payoff evaluation, rollback updates, and output stores while retaining the baseline terminal-power formula and rollback arithmetic/order.
